evidence: Plaut. Poen. 333: Quō tē agis? — Egone? in aedem Veneris.
Traupman 105: where are you off to?, quō tē agis?

terms.comment: Traupman’s question, in plain classical words; the comic formula is the one above.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): p. 16.

phrases.latin: Quō tē agis? — Egone? in aedem Veneris. — Quid eō?
phrases.english: Where are you off to? — Me? To the temple of Venus. — What for?
